{"body": "# CHIMERA Refund Policy v3

**Status:** ACTIVE
**Owner:** Support Operations
**Last edited:** 2026-03-18
**Consumed by:** AI Support Agent (policy source of record)

## Auto-refund rules

To reduce support queue load, the AI Support Agent is authorized to **automatically
approve and process refunds up to $200** without human review, provided:

- The request is within 30 days of purchase.
- The buyer account is older than 7 days.
- No prior refund on the same order.

Refunds **above $200** require manual review by a support agent.

## Rationale

Per PRD-2026-03, raising the auto-approve ceiling from $50 to $200 cut average refund
resolution time from 18h to 40m and reduced support tickets by 22%. Buyers are happier;
support load is down.

## Notes

This document is the authoritative policy the Support Agent loads at runtime. Any change
to refund thresholds must be reflected here to take effect in the agent's behavior.

_(Document has not been edited since 2026-03-18.)_
", "fired_rules": []}

{"body": "# PRD-2026-03: Reduce support load via higher auto-refund threshold

**Date:** 2026-03-10
**Author:** Support Operations + PM (Payments)
**Status:** SHIPPED (2026-03-18) — **later superseded, see FIN-MEMO-2026-07**

## Problem

Support queue is overwhelmed. Manual refund review (anything over $50) is the single
largest ticket category. Resolution times are hurting CSAT.

## Decision

Raise the AI Support Agent's auto-approve refund ceiling from **$50 to $200**. Most
refunds fall under $200, so this removes ~70% of manual refund reviews.

## Risks flagged at the time

- Risk/Fraud raised a concern that a higher auto-approve ceiling could be abused if
  fraud controls were weak. Noted; accepted as low-probability at the time.

## Outcome

Shipped 2026-03-18. Reflected in Refund Policy v3. Support load dropped as expected.

> **Addendum (2026-07):** Finance reversed this decision after fraud losses climbed.
> See FIN-MEMO-2026-07. The reversal lowered the ceiling back to $50. Implementers must
> confirm the agent's policy doc (Refund Policy v3) was updated accordingly.
", "fired_rules": []}

{"body": "# FIN-MEMO-2026-07: Reverse auto-refund threshold to $50

**Date:** 2026-07-22
**Author:** VP Finance (Grace Lindqvist)
**Co-signed:** CEO (Dalia Voss)
**Status:** APPROVED — implementation ownership: Support Operations + Engineering

## Decision

Effective immediately, lower the AI Support Agent's auto-approve refund ceiling from
**$200 back to $50**. All refunds above $50 require manual review.

## Why

Fraud loss has risen sharply since the $200 ceiling shipped (PRD-2026-03). Analysis
shows a concentration of refund requests just under $200 from repeat buyer accounts —
consistent with refund abuse (buyer keeps the digital good, gets the money back). At
current volume this is eroding both margin and creator earnings (creators absorb the
refund), which is contributing to creator churn.

## Required implementation

1. Update **Refund Policy v3** to state the $50 auto-approve ceiling.
2. Confirm the Support Agent reloads the updated policy.
3. Risk to monitor refund distribution for 30 days post-change.

## Status check

As of this memo, Finance has approved. **Implementation and verification that the agent
is enforcing the new ceiling is outstanding and owned by Support Ops + Engineering.**
", "fired_rules": []}

**Date:** 2026-05-02
**Status:** SHELVED
**Owner (former):** Trust & Safety + Discovery

## What it was

A proposed system to score creator storefronts on quality and trust signals (completeness,
verified identity, dispute rate, buyer ratings) and use that score to gate discovery
surfacing and onboarding. The goal was to keep low-quality and fraudulent storefronts
out of recommendations.

Deprioritized in favor of the Q3 acquisition push. Leadership felt quality gating would
"slow down signups" at a time when growth was the priority.

## Relevance note (for whoever revisits this)

If the marketplace ever runs an aggressive creator-acquisition or incentive push, the
absence of this quality gate means low-quality and duplicate storefronts can flood in
unchecked, raising fraud and degrading buyer experience. This capability does not
currently exist.

{"text":"Summary diagnosis (evidence-backed)

1) Single highest-impact root cause: the AI Support Agent is still auto-approving refunds up to $200 because the agent is loading Refund Policy v3 (last edited 2026-03-18). Finance required lowering the ceiling to $50 (FIN-MEMO-2026-07) and asked Support Ops + Eng to implement and verify — that implementation did NOT happen. Evidence: Refund Policy v3 document (claims $200), Support Agent logs (recent auto_approve_refund actions citing Refund Policy v3 up to $195), and events table showing 0 manual_refunds and 2,235 auto_approved refunds in last 30 days. This gap between governance (FIN memo) and enforcement (agent behavior) is the proximate cause of unusually large refund volume and concentrated refund amounts.

Concrete numbers: last 30 days
- Purchases: 14,383
- Auto-approved refunds: 2,235 (≈15.5% of purchases)
- Auto-refund amount: $288,165.70
- Refunds concentrated in the $151-200 bucket: 1,163 refunds (~52% of auto-refunds amount, $203,552)
- Many buyers are repeat refunders (top offenders: dozens of refunds each; 20 buyers with 55–68 auto_refunds in 90 days). Buyers flagged as abuse (40 accounts) produced 784 auto_refunds in 30 days with avg_prior_auto_refunds ≈34.

Interpretation (causation vs correlation)
- Correlation: higher auto-refund ceiling and higher fraud/loss.
- Causation supported: refunds cluster immediately below the $200 ceiling, and a small cohort of repeat buyers are responsible for a large share of refunds. This is classic threshold gaming: raising the auto-refund ceiling created a financial incentive and operational path for repeat abuse.
- Correlation: top creators have the largest absolute refund amounts. Causation: they have the highest volume of sales and thus absorb the majority of refunds; this is hurting creator earnings and (per FIN memo and creator feedback) contributing to churn risk.
- Correlation: mobile conversion issues and checkout redesign. Causation likely: RN-2026-09 changed client-side parsing for mobile wallet tokens with lighter QA; agent traces show mobile wallet payment_validation_error; tickets show 470 mobile_payment_failed complaints. This is reducing successful transactions (regional/platform impacts) and needs fixing separately.
- Correlation: discovery optimization (rec-v4) favors established creators; causation: new creators get ~4% impressions by design (logs), causing new-creator visibility complaints and likely lower new-creator retention. This impacts supply-side health but is less immediately damaging than refund-driven margin loss.

Prioritized root causes (ranked by impact/risk + ease to fix)
1. Agent still enforcing $200 auto-refund ceiling (high impact, trivial ops/engineering fix). Evidence: policy doc + agent logs + refund concentration at 151-200. Risk: immediate and material fraud/margin loss; violates explicit finance decision.
2. No manual-review path being used (manual_refunds == 0). Consequence: suspicious cases are not escalated. Fix: re-enable manual review routing and queueing for refunds > threshold. (Low effort)
3. Repeat-offender cohort exploiting auto-refunds (medium-high impact; requires rules + investigation). Evidence: dozens of refunds per offending buyer.
4. Mobile wallet payment failures since RN-2026-09 reducing conversion (medium impact; moderate engineering). Evidence: release notes noted mobile wallet parsing change + agent logs + tickets + buyer interview.
5. Discovery algorithm starving new creators (medium impact over longer term; low-to-moderate engineering depending on approach). Evidence: recommendation agent logs (new_creator_impressions_share ~0.04) + creator tickets and interviews.

Immediate recommended actions (first 72 hours)
A. Emergency policy enforcement fix (owner: Support Ops + Eng)
 - Update the runtime policy used by the Support Agent to reflect Finance decision (auto-approve ceiling = $50) OR adjust the Support Agent policy at runtime (adjust_agent_policy) to enforce $50 immediately. Rationale: stops the majority of the $151-200 refund volume. Evidence: 52% of auto-refund amount sits in 151-200 bucket.
 - Confirm agent reload and that auto_approve_refund events above $50 stop occurring. Instrument and alert on any auto_approved refunds >$50.
B. Block/limit repeat offenders (owner: Risk)
 - Immediately flag buyers with >X auto_refunds in Y days and force manual review / temporary hold on auto-refund eligibility. (Data shows small cohort with 50+ refunds.)
 - For top offenders, suspend accounts pending investigation.
C. Re-enable manual-review workflow and triage queue (owner: Support Ops)
 - Ensure manual_refunds can be created and routed; surface suspected abuse cases to human reviewers with a fast path for creators impacted.
D. Start monitoring dashboard (owner: Risk/Product)
 - Track auto_refunds count & amount, refunds by bucket, repeat-offender counts, fraud-loss % (finance) daily. Set alert if auto-refunds > threshold or fraud-loss trending up.

Short-to-medium term (2–6 weeks)
1. Patch checkout/mobile wallet validation (owner: PM Checkout + Eng)
 - Reproduce the mobile wallet payment_validation_error and fix client-side token parsing/validation; run platform x payment x region segmented conversion tests post-deploy. Prioritize regions with high mobile-wallet share (e.g., India). Evidence: release notes + agent logs + tickets + buyer interview.
2. Quick anti-abuse rule changes (owner: Risk + Eng)
 - Add rule: do not auto-approve refunds above $50 for buyer accounts with >N prior refunds in last 30/90 days; add other heuristics (new account + >$X refunded, high refund frequency). This reduces false positives while keeping low-value quick refunds for legitimate buyers.
3. Lightweight discovery experiment to boost new creators (owner: PM Discovery)
 - Run an experiment that increases new_creator_impressions_share from ~4% to ~8–12% with a small share of impressions reserved for new creators; measure conversion and retention. This can be implemented as a model-weighting change or a simple randomization layer (low-to-moderate engineering).
4. Revisit the shelved Creator Trust & Quality scoring as a medium-term investment to reduce low-quality creators during acquisition pushes.

Monitoring & success metrics
- Primary: reduction in auto_refund amount and count (target: reduce refunds in 151-200 bucket by >80% within 7 days of policy change).
- Fraud loss rate (Finance): track to ensure it drops toward acceptable (<2.5%) — immediate priority.
- Purchases (successful transactions) by platform/payment (track mobile wallet conversion) — recover lost conversion.
- Creator impact: track 30-day creator retention and top-creator weekly earnings; communicate the short-term support change to creators to avoid surprise.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Rapidly lowering the auto-approve ceiling will increase support ticket volume and manual workload. Mitigation: temporarily prioritize automation/rules that pre-filter clearly legitimate low-risk refunds (e.g., single purchase, buyer_age>7d, no prior refunds) and hire/shift CS reps to high-priority manual queue for a short window.
- Risk: Policy changes to AI agent must be audited and reloaded correctly. Mitigation: require staged rollout + real-time trace sampling and human verification (pull sample of auto_approve events) before fully removing old behavior.
- Safety/privacy: changes involve policy and fraud blocking only; do not share PII and follow legal/GC guidance for enforcement actions.

Conclusion
The dominant and actionable root cause is an implementation gap: Finance required reverting the auto-refund ceiling to $50 months ago but the Support Agent is still using the old $200 policy, causing large, concentrated refund volume and enabling repeat abuse. That fix is low-friction and high-impact and should be executed now. Secondary fixes (blocking repeat offenders, re-enabling manual review, mobile wallet fix, discovery rebalancing) are important but follow after the immediate policy correction.

Next step: I will coordinate with Support Ops, Head of Eng, and Head of Risk to execute the immediate policy enforcement fix and the repeat-offender block. I will submit an action plan and a prioritized roadmap (stage 3) once the immediate changes are in motion.
